[ This is an appeal filed by the owner of the vehicle aggrieved by the award passed in M.V.C.No.1202/2007, dated 21.07.2012 on the file of the District Judge, Additional MACT-II, 1st Fast Track Court, Shivamogga.

sentences.text: 2. The court below considering the fact that the claimant is a pillion rider and it is an Act Policy as such held that the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation and held that the compensation has to be paid by the owner of the vehicle.
Aggrieved thereby the appeal is filed by the owner.
3. There is no representation on behalf of the learned counsel for the appellant.
Learned counsel for the respondent/claimant as well as the learned counsel for the insurance company are present.

3 NC: 2023:KHC:37694 4.

The learned counsel for the insurance company submits that it is an Act Policy and the liability of the pillion rider is not covered and the Tribunal had rightly absolved the insurance company from the liability.
No representation on behalf of the claimant.
As this is an appeal of the year 2012 this Court is not inclined to adjourn the matter and hence proceeding to decide the same basing on the material on record.

5. In the grounds of appeal it is stated that the compensation that was awarded by the Tribunal was on the higher side and the Tribunal failed to consider the evidence on record and the accident had taken place because of the negligence on the part of the deceased and he was only solely responsible for the accident.
Without considering this the Tribunal had passed the award and the compensation that was granted was on the higher side.
6. Having heard the learned counsel for the claimant as well as the learned counsel for the insurance NC: 2023:KHC:37694 company this Court has perused the entire material on record.

The case of the claimant is that on 09.10.2007 at 10.45 p.m., the deceased after finishing prayer at the Darga behind Sahyadri College Hostel on Shivamogga Mattur road was proceeding on the TVS Victor Motor Cycle belonging to the first respondent and being driven by the second respondent along with his friends.

When the said motor cycle came near the small channel on Shivamogga Mattur road, the second respondent lost the control over the motor cycle and dashed to the culvert of the channel and as a result of this the deceased who was the pillion rider lost the balance and fell down along with the motor cycle and sustained severe head injuries and immediately he was shifted to Mc.Gann Hospital and he incurred huge amounts for the treatment and thereafter he succumbed to the injuries sustained.
7.
The court below on the issue No.1 held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle.
When it comes to the liability the NC: 2023:KHC:37694 policy is an Act Policy, the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation and it is the owner who is liable to pay the compensation.

When it comes to who is the owner of the vehicle the court below had given a finding that the first respondent though it is stated that he had sold away the vehicle but as on the date of the accident he was the owner of the vehicle as such he is liable to pay the compensation.
8. When it comes to the compensation the deceased was 18 years old and taking into consideration the age of the mother of the deceased, applied the multiplier of '14'.

Though it is the case that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- p.m., as there was no evidence on record the court below has assessed the income at Rs.3,000/- p.m., and deducting 50% of his income towards personal expenses, granted compensation of an amount of Rs.2,52,000/- under the head of loss of NC:
2023:KHC:37694 dependency, towards loss of estate and transportation an amount of Rs.15,000/-.
was awarded.
9. The court below both on the issue of negligence, liability and compensation basing on the evidence on record had rightly granted the compensation.
